title: the in-place Reed-Solomon decode writes its parity bytes at a fixed offset past the output buffer
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8 carries the fix's renamed constant PFT_RS_K_MAX and the widened allocation 'wmem_alloc(pinfo->pool, decoded_size + PFT_RS_N - rsk)' at :407, and the vulnerable 'memcpy(output+index_out+PFT_RS_N_MAX, ...)' has zero occurrences there. The triage script found 6 of 6 of the fix's distinctive added lines already in v4.6.8. A fix-reversal. The pre-fix shape is quoted from e8ef9df09d^:epan/dissectors/packet-dcp-etsi.c:235-237 (the swapped constants), :264 (the parity copy), :270 (index_out += rsk) and :376 (the allocation).
object: the RS output buffer, fcount*plen bytes in the packet scope
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial row.
shape: fixed-offset parity write lands past the buffer, inside the same block
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. The RS decode is reduced to the FIRST byte its parity copy writes past the buffer (index_out = 0, offset PFT_RS_N_MAX); eras_dec_rs and the deinterleave are dropped because they do not touch the bound.
distinguishing: the first row in this corpus whose stale access is a WRITE rather than a read, so it is the one that exercises the write probe and oracle_site's site-1 path.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'declined'.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.
native-detect.prediction: NO ASan report: the crossing stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks to poison. A silent arm needs its own positive control -- a crossing past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- before it means anything.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-libc/run-asan.txt: SILENT, the defect reproduced; wmem built with WM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON (g_malloc/g_free are the host's malloc/free); wmem's own control 90 reported heap-use-after-free at wm_probe in the same run. The earlier reading (2026-10-09) ran the hosted bump arena, which could read nothing else.

native-fix-differential.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-differential/: the buggy sequence reaches storage outside its object (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, exit 0) and the fixed sequence -- this case's upstream fix, modelled in case.c under wm_fixed -- does not (VERDICT FIXED, exit 0). Hosted build, upstream wmem allocator (WM_CHUNKS=OFF), `program 0 N buggy|fixed` (runners/run-native.sh). Spatial: the access address lies outside [object, object+size) in the buggy sequence and inside it, or is not made, in the fixed one. The arm did not exist before 2026-10-09: the cases had no fixed sequence.
